messages:
Maya: Quick sync — customer asks are piling up for the Console "insights" beta. They want: cost breakdown per-route, tracing hook one-liners, and a small set of dashboard templates for cost/error/latency. Can we define beta gating criteria and a minimal scope we can commit to for next sprint?
Liam: Agree we should be conservative. Suggested minimal scope: 1) cost per-route (simple token & compute attribution), 2) tracing hooks that capture request-id + model-variant, 3) three dashboard templates (customer summary, error trends, hot routes).
Zoe: From SRE POV the tracing hook needs to be low-overhead. We should instrument at request ingress and emit a small structured event to our trace collector. Example snippet: ```headers['X-Request-ID'] || generateUUID()``` and attach model_variant tag.
Anita: We'll need sample datasets to validate cost attribution accuracy. Ops: what's acceptable error bound on per-route cost? Customers will compare to their internal billing.
Maya: Good point. Proposal: per-route cost estimate within 10% of actual monthly spend for top 80% routes (by volume). If we can't hit that, we call it "preview" not beta.
Sam: UX asks: dashboards should be copy/paste ready. Minimal widgets: 1) cost by route (7d/30d), 2) median & p95 latency by route, 3) error rate trend with link to traces. Also a quick "how to onboard" panel.
Liam: Implementation notes: cost = tokens*unit_cost + gpu_seconds*gpu_rate (approx). We'll surface both token-only and total cost toggles. We can compute on ingest (streaming) or offline via daily aggregation. Streaming will give near-real-time but adds compute.
Zoe: For beta, prefer daily aggregation (lower ops risk) and a nightly job that computes per-route totals. Real-time can be V2.
Maya: Beta gating checklist (draft):
- Instrumentation: tracing hook implemented in runtime + docs
- Accuracy: per-route cost estimates within 10% for top 80% routes (measured across 3 pilot customers)
- Observability: three dashboard templates + one curated alert (error spike)
- Performance: tracing hook adds <1% p99 latency in internal perf test
- Onboarding: migration guide + sample config + 3 pilot customers committed
If any of these fail, we fall back to "preview" label.
Anita: For the accuracy requirement we need two pilot customers with diverse workloads (short chat vs batch embeddings). I can run backfills and compare nightly aggregates to their billing exports. Need their consent to map IDs.
Liam: Ownership: Eng runtime will add hook + emit structured trace. Eng-platform will add aggregation pipeline and dashboard templates. Maya owns pilot coordination and acceptance.
Deploy Bot: deployment queued for branch feature/console-insights-hook (diff: 7 files).
Sam: One small UX question — do we show raw estimated dollars or normalized units? Customers asked for both. I vote both: show $ and an explainable "units" breakdown (tokens, GPU secs).
Zoe: Alerts: propose a default error-rate alert (5xx rate > 1% for 15m) and a cost-alert (route cost > historical mean * 3 for 24h) — we'll tune later.
Maya: Next steps: Liam + Zoe to produce a short tech spec (one pager) by EOD Wednesday, Anita to list candidate pilot customers by Thursday, Sam to draft dashboard wireframes by Friday. I'll consolidate gating doc and share for signoff. :thumbsup:
Liam: Will do. Adding a tiny config sample for tracing hook: ```trace.enabled: true
trace.tags: [route, model_variant, request_id]
trace.emit_interval: nightly // beta```
Anita: Adding pilot candidates: Acme AI (chat), Vectorly (embeddings), FinProd (low-volume enterprise). Reaching out now.
Sam: I'll post the dashboard mock in #design after lunch.
Maya: Thanks team. If we hit all gating items, target beta rollout to pilots in 2 sprints. If not, we'll ship a preview label and open a follow-up sprint for real-time and accuracy improvements.
Zoe: One last ask — add a small perf test scenario (1000 concurrent short-chat reqs) so we can measure the <1% p99 overhead claim.
Liam: Adding perf test to sprint ticket.
Maya: Closing loop here — will create tracking ticket and link back. Thanks.
